$comment: Expectations for `pnpm canary:isolation`. Each key of `mutants` is a model the tenant-scope
extension isolates (plus `all`, which isolates nothing), and `mustFail` names the isolation-lane
cases that MUST go red once that model is no longer scoped. A named case that stays green is a
surviving mutant: the lane cannot see that model leaking, which is a hole in the lane.
Names are jest full names (the describe chain plus the title), so renaming a case here is caught
as "no such case in the run" rather than silently weakening the canary.
Every model in TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS must have an entry (lint:meta rule isolation-canary-coverage).

workspace.why: The first scoped model and the one every other tenant read hangs off.
mustFail: tenant isolation (live DB, app-layer extension is the only boundary) T1 scoped read isolation: findMany returns only the active tenant rows
tenant isolation (live DB, app-layer extension is the only boundary) T2 scoped findUnique by cross-tenant id resolves to null
every model the extension isolates has a cross-tenant case workspace C1 a row of tenant A is invisible to a scoped read under tenant B

all.why: The registry never loaded at all: the accessor-mapping refactor that makes every lookup miss.
mustFail: every model the extension isolates has a cross-tenant case workspace C1 a row of tenant A is invisible to a scoped read under tenant B
tenant isolation (live DB, app-layer extension is the only boundary) T1 scoped read isolation: findMany returns only the active tenant rows
